notes: Interface method (Interface5), implemented by GL and D3D vertex/index buffer wrapper classes (GlBufferObject, GlIndexBufferArb, GlVertexBufferArb, D3dIndexBuffer, D3dVertexBuffer). All implementations return a cached byte-count field representing the buffer's current uploaded data size (GlBufferObject: `return anInt4747`, the field written by method2121/method23 whenever data is uploaded/resized; D3dIndexBuffer: `return anInt8516`; D3dVertexBuffer: `return anInt8508`), confirming this is a 'get current size in bytes' getter -- matches the interface name SizedResource. The `bool` parameter, when true, triggers an extra call before returning: GlBufferObject calls `method2122(127)` (a private helper that, for that specific argument, always hits its early-return branch and discards the result -- a dead/no-op decoy, since the guard `i != 27819` is always true for 127); D3dIndexBuffer calls `method25(116.toByte())` and D3dVertexBuffer calls `method3519(-55)` (both side-effecting native/GL calls whose results are likewise discarded). GlIndexBufferArb's override is notably suspicious: `if (bool != false) method16(true)` followed by `return super.method16(false)` -- if bool is ever true, this recurses into itself with `true` again, which would recurse infinitely (stack overflow), so this branch is a latent bug/dead-code path; the only real call site found (NativeRenderer.kt:426, `anInterface5_Impl2_8195!!.method16(false)`) always passes `false`, so the recursive branch is never actually exercised. Net effect: treat `bool` as a best-effort 'flush/refresh before reporting size' flag per the pattern, but flag that it is unverified/unused-in-practice and one implementation would crash if it were ever set true.
